Scheme 
  The Tamil Nadu Official Language Act, 1956 
was enacted on December, 27 th 1956 and 
published in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette

Tamil as the Language to be used for the official 
purposes of the State . The legislation has been 
enacted under the  Article 345 of the Constitution 
of India.  Under this Act, regular inspections are 
conducted to ensure that Tamil is actively use d in 
all Government departments and autonomous 
bodies. 
   Inspection activities are carried out to 
evaluate the implementation of the Official 
Language Scheme in Secretariat departments. In

departmental head offices, Boards and District 
Collectorates, inspections are conducted by the 
Director of Tamil Development.  In Subordinate 
Offices, inspection works are carried out by 
District-level Deputy Directors and Assistant 
Directors of Tamil Development. 
1.1.2 Inspection Procedure 
The Director of Tamil Developm ent along 
with the Zonal / District- level Deputy Directors 
and Assistant Directors of Tamil Development, 
prepare a list of offices to be inspected, devise a 
prior travel itinerary every month and 
systematically carryout the inspection works.  
Stages of the Inspection Procedure: 
• Prior Notice and Questionnaire:  
Information regarding the inspection, along 
with a detailed questionnaire for data 
compilation, will be sent in advance to the 
offices to be inspected.  The staff of the office 
7 
under inspection must co mplete the details 
regarding files and registers in the 
questionnaire and submit it to the officials of 
the Tamil Development Department on the 
day of inspection. 
• Physical Verification: Officials of the Tamil 
Development Department conduct physical 
verification regarding the details provided by 
the department being inspected and the 
usage of Tamil in employee’s documents.   
• Evaluation of Documents and Inspection 
Report: A comprehensive inspection shall be 
conducted regarding the usage of Tamil in all 
office documents. In the inspection report 
sent to the office following the inspection, 
areas of commendable performance as well 
as identified deficiencies will be explicitly 
highlighted.  A compliance report is obtained 
after the identified deficiencies are rectified.

1.1.3 Workshops on Official Language 
Workshops are conducted in all districts of 
Tamil Nadu to create awareness among 
Government officials and employees regarding the 
Official Language Scheme. These workshops 
impart awareness on subjects such as h istory and 
legislation of the official language, Government 
Orders, simplified implementation and digital 
Tamil computing. Participants receive certificates 
of participation. This scheme is being 
implemented with a financial allocation of 
Rs.50,000/- per district, amounting to a total of 
Rs.19,00,000/-. 
1.1.4 Seminars on Official Language 
  Official language seminars are conducted 
annually in every district for the employees of 
Government departments, autonomous 
institutions, Boards and C orporations.  Training is 
imparted in these seminars, through experts in 
9 
Tamil grammar and literature, alongside domain 
specialists. This scheme is implemented with a 
financial allocation of Rs.20,000/- per district, 
amounting to a total of Rs.7,60,000/-. 
1.1.5 Training on Official Language Scheme 
  Considering the large number of 
Government employees in Chennai district, 
additional training on Official Language Scheme is 
imparted exclusively to the employees serving in 
Government offices, Boards and Corporations 
within Chennai district.  In this two -day 
comprehensive training program, five training 
sessions of two days each are conducted with a 
financial allocation of Rs.1,50,000 (Rupees One 
Lakh and Fifty thousand only), covering core 
subjects including Official Language Act/History, 
Government Orders, Coinage of Terminologies, 
Translation, Preparation of Official Notes and 
Drafts and Inspection Procedures.

  The "Official Language Act Week" is 
observed annually from December 21 to 27  to 
emphasize the implementation of the Tamil 
Official Language Act among employees of 
Government offices, Boards and autonomous 
bodies across Tamil Nadu, as well as to create 
awareness among the general public and traders.

implement this scheme across districts through 
the Tamil Development Department with an 
allocation of Rs.1,00,000/- per district.
